subject: Per-call quantum tiering and long-history amortization — billing clarification
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@lynxhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify per-call rounding for long-history bundle

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look great. Procurement has one remaining question before we can sign the SOW: how does Redwood handle per-call rounding and minimums for calls that reference long conversation history (we keep ~30 days of context)? Two specific asks:

1) If a single API call references a 6k-token retained history + 600-token prompt, what is the billed unit? Do you round the full (history+prompt+response) to a quantum?

2) For our expected pattern (many short interactions with large retained history), will there be a long-history amortization or 'bucket' that prevents astronomical per-call charges?

We're trying to map this to our monthly model to compare to other offers. Would appreciate a short worked example we can show procurement.

Best,
Alex
Director of Platform 
LynxHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@lynxhealth.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify per-call rounding for long-history bundle

Alex — thanks for the clear question. Short answer: we bill on a token-quantum plus a small per-call microfloor; for long-history we apply an amortization policy that prevents paying the full retained-history cost on every short interaction. Below is a concise explanation and a simple worked example for your procurement team.

Policy highlights (high level):
- Quantum granularity: 250-token increments (we round up to the nearest 250 tokens for the billed unit).
- Microfloor: each API call carries a 500-token minimum billing floor (covers small control calls / heartbeats).
- Long-history amortization: retained context is amortized into a "history credit" bucket per conversation id. We apportion the retained-history cost across active calls to that conversation over a 30-day window. Practically that means most short replies won't see the full 6k-history cost repeatedly.

Worked example (your numbers):
- Actual tokens on call: history 6000 + prompt 600 + generated 1200 = 7800 total tokens.
- Round up to nearest 250 => billed tokens = ceil(7800 / 250) * 250 = 8000 tokens.
- Apply microfloor: billed tokens is max(8000, 500) => 8000.
- With history amortization: the 6000-history portion contributes a per-call amortized charge. If we amortize 6000 tokens over 30 days and you average 6 calls/day, effective per-call history charge = 6000 / (30 * 6) = ~33 tokens; we then include that in the per-call arithmetic before quantum rounding.

In short:, procurement will see that the amortization drastically reduces repeated full-history billing. I'll attach the CSV with the sample rows filled in and can convert the math into an SOW paragraph if you like.

Would you like us to update the SOW language to call out the 250-token quantum + 500-token microfloor + 30-day amortization? If so, I can loop legal and send a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Thanks,

Vanessa / Karthik — forwarding Lynx's procurement questions (above). They want: rationale for 250-token quantum and safe handling for bursty incident scenarios. I sketched a proposal below — please weigh in quickly so we can finalize SOW language.

Suggested stance / rationale:
- Why 250 tokens: it balances billing noise vs customer fairness. 100-token quantum creates larger invoice volatility and larger item counts; 1k-step is too coarse and penalizes small-medium calls. 250 is close to 256 (power-of-two beneficial for certain batching buffers) and keeps invoice lines manageable.
- Burst protection: implement a temporary "burst window" policy — if per-conversation call rate exceeds X calls/day (we use 5x baseline), switch to a short-window amortization recalculation (72-hour window) so cost reflects real burst amortization rather than charging full retained-history each call. This caps spike exposure. We track and surface the conversion in Console and apply invoice smoothing credits if threshold exceeded.

Sample invoice lines for Alex's profile (12k calls/month; 70% short replies):
- Calls: 12,000 API calls
- Short reply category (8,400 calls): typical pre-amortization tokens per call: prompt 200 + gen 60 + amortized-history 30 => 290 tokens => round up to 500 (250-quantum) => billed_token_sum_short = 8,400 * 500 = 4,200,000 tokens
- Long-reply category (3,600 calls): average 1,500 tokens per call => round up to 1,500 (already multiple of 250) => billed_token_sum_long = 3,600 * 1,500 = 5,400,000 tokens
- Total billed tokens = 9,600,000 tokens for month.

Notes: exact invoice numbers depend on sampling cadence and whether the 72-hour burst window kicks in; legal should be explicit that amortization buckets and burst windows are operational mechanisms and we will surface estimates in Console.

Decision needed: agree to 250-token quantum, 500-token microfloor, 30-day default amortization, and 72-hour burst amortization with console visibility. If yes, I'll ask Legal to add a short clause and send the updated SOW to Alex.

Thanks — Marissa

Alex — quick follow-up: legal has accepted the clause language and we've embedded the pricing rules into the SOW draft. Summary of what we will operationalize and what you will see on invoices/Console:

- Quantum: 250-token rounding (billed tokens always round up to nearest 250).
- Microfloor: 500-token minimum per call (applies before monthly aggregation).
- Amortization: default 30-day amortization for retained history per conversation id; amortized tokens will be calculated daily and applied to calls referencing that conversation.
- Burst protection: if a conversation's call rate spikes >5x typical baseline, a 72-hour amortization recalculation is used to avoid per-call shock billing; Console will flag and list affected conversation ids.

I've attached the SOW (LynxHealth_SOW_v1.pdf) with the new paragraph and a sample invoice export. Please review. If it looks good, sign here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-lynx-sow and we'll cut the order.
